- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -1.95 or below) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to reflect momentum decay.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.65) and model is forecasting a downtrend, check for lag: true price often reverses within 3–5 days; shift forecast horizon to align with recent 10–15 day mean.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., 0.65+), model tends to overestimate upside; cap forecast at 10–15% below recent 30-day high to avoid overbought bias.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., 70–72 range vs true 72–74), sentiment history may be underweighting risk; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is flat or mildly positive.
